answerNotes.SCENT: Scent means a smell, often a pleasant one. Flower scents vary, and not every colorful bloom has a strong fragrance.
answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.
answerNotes.CLOTH: Cloth means fabric. A cloth used for wiping is an object made from that material, not a different substance.
answerNotes.RIBBON: A ribbon is a narrow fabric strip. A looped bow and a straight trailing tail are different parts of a tied ribbon decoration.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.
answerNotes.FLOWER: A flower is the blossom, rather than the whole plant. In everyday speech, the word can also describe a plant grown for its blooms.
answerNotes.THREAD: Thread is usually finer than knitting yarn. It passes through a sewing needle's eye to form stitches.
answerNotes.NEEDLE: A sewing needle has a point and an eye. Knitting needles generally use pointed ends to form loops without threading an eye.
answerNotes.SEAM: A seam joins pieces of fabric. A hem finishes an edge instead of joining two separate pieces.
answerNotes.DRAWER: A drawer slides in and out of furniture. Its front may have a handle, while dividers separate the contents inside.

answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.

answerNotes.FALL: Fall is the usual American word for autumn. Both name the season after summer and before winter.
answerNotes.STEM: A stem supports leaves and flowers. It also connects the plant's growing parts with the roots below.

answerNotes.HANG: Hang means support something from above. A hook, cord, or branch can hold the weight while the object hangs below.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
